rules.title: NJ Law Against Discrimination – source of lawful income / rent payment
rules.requirement: A landlord cannot refuse to rent to someone based on the source of lawful income or lawful rent payment, such as a Section 8 voucher.
rules.quoted_span: The LAD also prohibits housing discrimination  based on the source of lawful income or source of lawful rent or mortgage payment a tenant or purchaser uses.
rules.key_value: ban on source-of-income discrimination (incl. Section 8 vouchers)
rules.exemptions: Rental of a single apartment in a two-family dwelling where the owner occupies the other unit; rental of rooms by owner/occupant of a one-family dwelling they occupy; religious organization preference.

unverifiable_exemptions: room rental in owner-occupied one-family dwelling

parsed.doc_summary: NJ Division on Civil Rights brochure on the Law Against Discrimination in housing. It states the ban on source-of-income discrimination, such as Section 8 vouchers, which is the only in-scope rule. It says nothing on rent, eviction, deposits, fees or algorithmic pricing.
